cells.tense: What you hold is already moving to the people who need it, and it moves cleanly — you can feel it land.
cells.ask: Offer the next piece you've been keeping for when it's perfect, still unfinished, and let the giving set your direction.
cells.core:
What's given here fits what's needed. Nothing piles up on the shelf, and the people who leave carry something they can actually use. You add what you have, it gets used, and more comes back through the same door. The whole thing runs without much deciding.

What's ready to grow is the choosing underneath it. Handing things along is second nature by now — that part steers itself — but the aim behind the giving is still borrowed a little, still safe. Pick where all this strength is actually pointed, and say it plainly. The giving keeps moving either way. Naming its direction is what makes it yours.
cells.sheetLine: What you carry is moving to the people who need it, and now you get to aim it.
cells.verb: lending your strength where the common work needs it
cells.place: in what gets handed down and shared

cells.tense: You're already bracing against a moment nobody can write in yet — planning the delivery before the need has spoken.
cells.ask: Name where the line is and hold it once this week, even knowing someone might be unhappy about it.
cells.core:
There's a room that knows how things get passed down, how teaching turns into tradition, when it works: what's given fits what's needed, and nothing piles up. People leave carrying something they can actually use.

But the giving has outrun the needing. You're deciding what everyone should receive before they've said what they need, weighing it all yourself, ahead of time, and then handing it over like a verdict. What sets the weight down is not more pushing — it's the plain inner measure of what's owed and what isn't. Name where the line is and hold it once, choose the give that's fair over the give that's complete, and the carrying gets lighter.
cells.sheetLine: You're deciding what everyone needs before they've said a word.

cells.place: in what gets handed down and shared

cells.tense: Something you gave away is still being weighed at a door you're standing in front of, and the giving's gone quiet.
cells.ask: Finish one thing you've been half-done with, badly, and count it as done instead of waiting for it to feel finished.
cells.core:
The work of carrying what's worth keeping wants to look like a load that fits the hands it reaches — easy in, easy out, both sides knowing it's right. What happens instead is the giving keeps getting weighed, and the weighing has settled where the offering used to be. You start calling this just how things are, holding what you have close, waiting for a signal everyone else seems to have.

Held-back strength doesn't stay neutral; it drags on the whole line. Pushing yourself back through the door won't do it. Finish one thing outright and let it be done. Small is fine. Half-good is fine. Finished things release on their own, and that release is what gets the strength moving again.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped giving, and it isn't a wall — it's a season you haven't closed.
cells.verb: lending your strength where the common work needs it
cells.place: in what gets handed down and shared

cells.tense: There's a hand behind the passing-down that keeps working while you talk about it like weather.
cells.ask: Say out loud which of the things you've been handing down you already chose on purpose, and say it as yours.
cells.core:
The way this works when it works is a visible hand in the settling: someone picks what's worth handing on and gives it on purpose. That's going on here, but the credit has been given quietly to the culture, the times, the way things are now — as if you're just reporting what's already true.

So the work is returning to the simpler, earlier form of the same act: pick one thing you're passing down and call it chosen. Say it out loud as yours — no heat in it, no case to make, just the hand resting visibly on what it inherited. The weight of an authored gesture lands differently than a habit does, and that difference is the whole point.
cells.sheetLine: The passing-down is already running. You just haven't signed it.
